items.note: K1 states the signed exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch value restored, and K1.a.1-K1.b follow the proof at 741-765 step by step: net change (JV+RG)x, central coefficients |S cap T| mod 2 and (|S cap T|-1)/2, and the three-stage composition. The network's size (h=100, triple-indexed banks, N, m) and the wire counts W_b, W_c (767-781) are not given.

K2 gives D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} with edge changes D_vD_u^{-1} and a common frame per gate. K2.a-K2.c reproduce the paper's invariant: true at sources, carried by edges, commuting with pointwise gates, and giving eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} on each route, auxiliary roles included.

The budget Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich, the single decreasing central edge losing h, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539 are all stated, and the telescoping at gates (1066-1071) is shown. The labels themselves are never built: the plan has no bilinear forms, no triple indicator vectors with orthogonal neighbouring lines, no F^{tensor 3}, no terminal or gate label tables and no residual table. Nestedness and the location of the decreases are only quoted from the lemma (K3.A.2), and the orthonormal-basis part over F_2 is omitted.

The plan has the rank sum s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b<W_bm, the shear frames Phi_M and the endpoint identity giving H<-H+D on every role (KS.frame). It shows how the rank sum is obtained: P_V-P_U has rank equal to the dimension change, and the -P_{U_a} sources contribute N extra ranks. The endpoint identity is only asserted. The paper's check that P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m and that every other role goes from zero to identity (1169-1171) is missing, and the assignment of P_U to gates and sinks is only implicit.

The plan states the edge frame change as one translation kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s_c calls, and C^{tensor e} on every role after corrections. It never defines the phase frames C_U=H^{tensor m} diag(i^{q_U}) H^{tensor m} or gives s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c<W_cm. Nothing of the proof appears (weight additivity mod 4, the Hadamard conversion of characters to translations, the C^{-1} factors on the 27 support coordinates fixed by Z wrappers); the sub-steps quote the later restatements at 1840, 1905 and 1912.

For the bit network the chain is complete: L_b/N<1/2, deficit N-2L_b>0, relative deficit >20*2^{-50}, log m<20, hence s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} (1331-1343). The exact eta values are not given. The complex saving (deficit 2N-2L_c, s_c<W_cm, s_c/W_c<m^sigma) is never derived, although S3.3 uses a<=m^sigma.

S2.1 lists the elementary O(V) operations correctly. S2.2 leaves out the hypothesis that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time and the conditions on q and the coefficients. Its one-line method fits only the offset update. Neither step goes through a proof.

Both statements are right: A=E_1 Pi E_2 with exactly a ones, and the shear with exactly rank(A) interchanges plus O(V). K5.a-K5.c follow the cost proof (1425-1446). The elimination proof of the factorization (1375-1392) is absent, since K4 is a bare infer step, and so is the choice of a fixed odd prime q avoiding the table's denominators (1413-1423).

Every step of the paper's proof is present. The base case and the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W come first. Then come the Phi_M frames with the endpoint condition giving H<-H+D, the three-update swap, s recursive calls, and F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) solved by the geometric sum in both cases a<=1 and a>1. The depth-first parking schedule and the descriptor bound complete it. The W^k row requirement appears in S2 and S2.3 rather than in KS itself.

The plan follows the paper's outline: high digits supply rows, padding to a multiple of W^k, base-m pieces, cost O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), and binary padding to [q^e]. It omits the essential layout step: joining h^+ after d^+ so that a row field of range q^{2 rho}>=W^k precedes both remaining chunks, then separating them again (1660-1680, 1708-1712). It also omits how rho is chosen for this.

The plan has s_c forward child calls of C^{tensor f} on slots of f axes, inverse children from (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. The central device is missing. The binary change of basis P_M with P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv} turns residual directions into coordinate slots (eq:phase-edge-coordinate), and Gaussian elimination splits it into a fixed number of row additions. The plan mentions 'binary changes of basis' only by name.

All steps of the proof appear. The eight conditional additions give the net map (u+c(1-2(u mod 2)),w). Each line becomes one cyclic chunk shift. The guard union bound gives delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}. T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes B, which is repaired by radix sort, and a final two-bit XOR handles the last position. The cost is given in its family form O(V(L^tau+1)).

The plan has the node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), rows from the first q_0 chunks with 2^{q_0K}>=W^{k_0}, children of volume V/W, and the recurrence with leaves O(e). The sums follow: internal nodes O(e^lambda), leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), base-m pieces, and the condition on lambda'. This matches 2286-2445.

The plan states the layer, exact evaluation with one truncation, O(Vd^{lambda'}) and error <sqrt2 2^{-p}. It follows the guard-width argument: A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, depth-l values in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] of modulus <=2^l, and epsilon C_1<1 giving Delta=o(p). It ends with the row-sum-one disk argument. K=floor(d^c) and the parameter bands are not restated in S3.

Character cancellation, decimation in frequency into bit-reversed storage B_t, the reversed procedure F_t^+B_t^{-1}, layout L with exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, cost and error all follow the paper. S4.3's claim that 'every round is one simultaneous layer' is loose: prefix-slot rounds are done bit by bit, as S4.3.b itself says.

The plan evaluates at B_0=2^{4p}, uses the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2 with centered extraction and carry in {0,1}, then forms the ac-be, ae+bc streams, reduces them mod y^r+1 and shifts by p+l. This is the paper's proof.

Both forward transforms are kept in LB order and multiplied pointwise, followed by the opposite transform and the exact scale M. The plan has the normalization identity, P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), and the error 3 delta+eta scaled to sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, as in 3414-3473.

The route follows 3576-3642 and 3836-3889: the Gaussian identity, N=CTD invertible by a Neumann series, B_0=D'J'C, the normalization product 2^{-2 alpha^2}, tensoring, line costs and axis exposure. The statement never defines P_s, P_t ((P_su)_j=u_{tj}, (P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}), and the hypotheses gcd(s,t)=1 and theta>p/alpha^4 and the error bound p^2 are not attached to the resampling step.

Both identities and the three proof steps match 3938-3983: the coefficient check, RF_s^+R=F_s^+ from the unit substitution, and the convolution rule with its normalizations. The chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) is never defined.

The fixed exponents, sizes, prime intervals with eta=1/(4d), T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p and the no-wraparound bound are all correct. Some checks are missing: the layer and dimension conditions (tau(1+c/beta)<lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)<lambda'<1, the epsilon conditions; 4018-4036), the comparison constants a_d, b_d, a_r, b_r, and the n^{o(1)} prime search.

The plan shows Phi is an isomorphism (image of x has order S), gives the triangular coordinate formula b_i, updates in order i=d..1 by controlled shifts, and costs the padding and O(d^2) axis swaps, as in the paper.

Well-definedness, the diagonal isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T follow 4303-4347. The computed twist errors of 4 appear in S6.6.b.

The source transform (A, chirp, B_0, scale 2^gamma, conjugate for F^+) and the six steps match the paper, including the meaning of the two scales by S. The input scale 2^{-b-2} is implicit only, through 'norm below 1/4' and 2^{2b+4}.

The plan tracks E_ring<5TL, the twisted convolution <6TL, the chirp <8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL and E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, then the final error <448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2 using gamma<=b/4. Rounding, the carry recurrence and the 2n-bit output follow, as in the paper.

The plan gives all seven table rows with their powers, the margins with min g_i=g_2=2^{-181}=2 kappa, the row justifications, setup at most p^{A+C}=o(Tp), log-power absorption, the total O(Tp p^{1-kappa}) and the schoolbook cutoff. It only names the exceptional-stream sorting bound as lower order.
S0 names 'n-log-n-conjecture' only in its relies-on list. No step states the eventual lower bound or argues that O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) forces T_A(n)/(n lg n)->0.

errors.says: Adding an offset to a later target field modulo q^b, or multiplying it by a fixed unit, costs O(V) by splitting each fibre into two pieces and merging them in the opposite order.
errors.paper: The two-piece split and opposite-order merge is the method for the offset (574-583), and it needs the offset to be preparable in b^{O(1)} time (566). Multiplication by a unit c splits each fibre into c increasing pieces merged by a residue counter, and negation uses a stack reversal (592-614).

errors.says: The layout L puts the selected bits of all axes at a common offset in K-bit chunks, so every round is one simultaneous layer.
errors.paper: Only the rounds on the remaining chunks use the simultaneous layer (3071-3104). The leading round on the long axes and the bottom positions h=b-1..0 are prefix-slot rounds processed bit by bit at cost O(TpdK) (3058-3062, 3106-3128). S4.3.b agrees with the paper here, so this is a loose summary.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: digit convolution, the bit-network chunk swap (K1-K10, S2.3-S2.6), the complex-network butterfly layer (S3), synthetic transforms and ring convolution (S4), Gaussian resampling with chirp and permutation cancellation (S5), exact recovery (S6) and the cost table with min margin 2 kappa (S7). It thins out where the networks are built. The subspace labels (bilinear forms, triple indicator vectors, label and residual tables) and the bit endpoint identity are asserted rather than constructed. On the complex side the phase-frame interface, its s_c<W_cm and sigma, and the P_M change of basis are taken as given, so the butterfly layer's saving rests on unproved steps.

steps.note: K1 has a fixed linear network on two banks, built from a three-element-subset gadget, that sends (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restores every scratch value. The defining parameters never appear: h=100, banks indexed by triples a in T^3, N=binom(100,3)^3 and m=h^3. N and m are later used in K3 without definition, so the step is only partly reconstructed and is judged mentioned.

A common invertible frame per gate commutes with a pointwise gate, the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and only the edge changes D_vD_u^{-1} cost anything. KS.frame instantiates this with the frames Phi_M.

Gates and terminals get nested nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space, every edge joins comparable labels, and the only decreasing edges are the Ic central edges from time 3 to 4, each losing h. The construction of the labels from triple indicators is absent, but the table's defining content is carried.
For nondegenerate U in V, P_V-P_U is the identity on V cap U^perp, with rank dim V-dim U. The N source edges, whose matrix is 2P_{U_a}, are the rank-one exceptions.
Source dimensions sum to N and sink dimensions to Wm-N, which gives Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich. Adding N source ranks gives s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 are both below 1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 and s_b<W_bm.
KS.frame states M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m and concludes H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included. The verification P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m is not shown, but the identity and its role are carried.

A rank-a matrix factors as E_1 Pi E_2. Triangular parts are linear-cost controlled shifts, and each one of Pi costs one interchange, so the cost is exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Hence s recursive calls per node.
Children have volume V/W, F_0=O(1) and F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). From eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 the plan gets s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, and the geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the chain behind the central saving along the bit-network branch. It covers frames (K2), labels whose only decreases are the central 3->4 edges (K3.A.2), rank equal to dimension change with rank-one source exceptions (K3.B.2-3), the budget and s_b (K3.A.1, K3.B.1), the 100/539 ratio and positive deficit (K3.A.3, K3.B.4), the endpoint shear (KS.frame), rank-a shears costing a interchanges (K4, K5, KS.count), and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50} (K3.C, K10). Eight of nine steps are reconstructed. Only C1 falls short: the network's concrete parameters (h=100, triple-indexed banks, N and m) are never given.
